title: Chairman, West Bengal State Electricity Board & Ors. v. Syed Mukbul Hossain & Ors.
coram: Arijit Pasayat & Mukundakam Sharma, JJ. (delivered by Arijit Pasayat, J.)
docket: Civil Appeal (arising out of SLP (C) No. 6618 of 2007)
disposition: Appeal disposed of (costs set aside; statutory appeal to be decided on merits)
headnote: Where, after a provisional assessment for theft/meter-tampering, supply is disconnected under the West Bengal Electricity Supply Code Regulation 5.2 and a final assessment is made under Section 126, the consumer's remedy is the statutory appeal under Section 127 against the final order, to be decided on merits by the appellate authority — including any objection as to the maintainability/limitation of that appeal. The Supreme Court set aside the High Court's imposition of costs and directed the appeal to be decided in accordance with law without being influenced by the observations below, expressing no opinion on merits.

holding_units.code: West Bengal Electricity Regulatory Commission (Electricity Supply Code) Regulations, 2004
holding_units.topic: Disconnection procedure and the statutory route of objection/appeal under ss.126-127
holding_units.holding: Disconnection of supply on a theft allegation must follow the procedure of Regulation 5.2; the consumer's remedies are to object under Section 126(3) before the final assessment and to appeal the final order under Section 127. As the final assessment had already been made, the Court relegated the parties to the statutory appeal, to be decided on merits (including the maintainability/limitation objection), setting aside the costs and interim directions of the High Court and expressing no opinion on merits.
holding_units.flag: Multi-state: construes the West Bengal Supply Code (2004), not the U.P. 2005 Code. The Supreme Court expressly decided nothing on the merits.

principle_tags.application: Where the statutory appeal under Section 127 against a final assessment is available and has been invoked, the parties are relegated to it (with maintainability/limitation left to the appellate authority) rather than to writ/appellate interference on merits.

not_decided.point: Merits and maintainability of the statutory appeal
not_decided.note: The Court expressly expressed no opinion on merits; the maintainability of the appeal on the ground of alleged delay was left to the appellate authority.
